subject: CirrusCare private endpoints & on-prem implementation orchestration
messages:
From: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@cirruscare.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>; Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <atorres@cirruscare.com>, it@cirruscare.com
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Implementation kickoff + network diagram (private endpoints / on-prem)

Hi Irene / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward with a private deployment. Attached is our current network diagram and a short list of infra constraints. Before our kickoff, we want to confirm a few items so we can scope the on-prem package and VPC peering correctly:

- Primary CIDR ranges we intend to use (see diagram) and whether overlapping subnets are acceptable for split-horizon DNS.
- Preferred connectivity: VPC peering vs Transit Gateway / Direct Connect.
- Whether outbound egress must traverse an on-prem firewall (we have a centralized egress proxy).
- Expected throughput for canary traffic (we can start small but want estimates).

Could you confirm who will own the peering setup vs who configures our firewall rules? Also propose 1-hour blocks for a technical kickoff (US-Pacific preferred).

Attachments: cirruscare_network_diagram_v1.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Claire Zhao
Head of IT Operations
CirrusCare
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@cirruscare.com>; Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff + network diagram (private endpoints / on-prem)

Claire — thanks for the diagram and questions. Monica and I reviewed it and put together a high-level implementation checklist (attached) and a few follow-ups below. We can own coordination for the VPC peering and provisioning of the Redwood Private control-plane artifacts; CirrusCare will need to provision the peering on your cloud side and confirm firewall/NAT rules.

High-level answers / asks:
- Overlapping CIDRs: we prefer non-overlapping by default. If split-horizon is required we’ll need explicit DNS routing rules and a test plan for name resolution.
- Connectivity: we recommend Transit Gateway if you plan to have many spokes or cross-account routing; we can peer directly for a single VPC-to-VPC connection. Please advise expected number of spokes.
- Egress: if all outbound must go through your firewall, we'll need a list of allowed destination IPs and FQDNs for the private endpoints so your policy team can allow them.
- Throughput: what does "small" mean? 50–200 req/s or token throughput? Give us an expected concurrency so we can size the canary.

Proposed kickoff slots (PST): Tue 6/5 10:00–11:00, Wed 6/6 13:00–14:00. Monica, Marcus, and Laura will join. I attached the Redwood provisioning playbook and a sample preflight checklist.

Attachments: redwood_provisioning_playbook_v2.md (MD)

Thanks — Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@cirruscare.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff + network diagram (private endpoints / on-prem)

Quick technical notes to add before the kickoff:

- MTU and path-MTU: if CirrusCare uses an on-prem appliance that performs encapsulation (VPN), confirm the MTU is 1400 or greater to avoid fragmentation with large token payloads.
- BGP / route propagation: for Transit Gateway/BGP setups, we will advertise a /24 per Redwood cluster. Please ensure route table limits allow these routes.
- Security groups: create an inbound rule for the private endpoint IPs we will publish (we'll provide exact IPs the week of the rollout).
- NAT vs SNAT: if you preserve source IPs for downstream services, we need to know whether SNAT will be applied.

I've opened JIRA INF-4821 to track infra pre-reqs and will add estimated IPs and ports there once we confirm the canary profile.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Network Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@cirruscare.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Torres <atorres@cirruscare.com>, it@cirruscare.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff + network diagram (private endpoints / on-prem)

Thanks + good questions. Answers below and a small update attached.

- CIDRs: Primary VPC: 10.10.0.0/16, Services VPC: 10.20.0.0/16. No overlapping plans.
- Spokes: just one additional spoke (analytics VPC) — direct peering sufficient for initial rollout.
- Egress: all outbound must pass through our centralized firewall/proxy. We'll provide an allowlist for IPs/FQDNs.
- Throughput: canary target ~80 req/s with burst to 200 for short periods. Start with 2 dedicated nodes for canary.
- MTU: our VPN appliance is set to 1420.

Attaching a short infra export with VPC IDs and contact for our network ops. We'll have our firewall team open a ticket after kickoff.

Attachments: cirruscare_vpc_export_20280605.json (attachment stub)

Claire
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhao <claire.zhao@cirruscare.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff + network diagram (private endpoints / on-prem)

Great — thanks for the answers Claire. Next steps and owners:

- CirrusCare network ops (Alex T.) to open firewall ticket with allowlist we provide — owner: Alex Torres (CirrusCare) — due: 2028-06-08
- Redwood (Marcus) to publish preliminary private endpoint IPs in JIRA INF-4821 — owner: Marcus Lin — due: 2028-06-07
- Redwood (Irene) to run provisioning runbook and share preflight checklist for canary — owner: Irene Choi — due: 2028-06-09
- Legal/admin: CirrusCare to return signed MSA (we've attached the most recent version) — owner: Claire — due: 2028-06-12

Canary plan summary: start with 2 nodes behind a dedicated private endpoint, validate auth/authz and end-to-end latency, then scale to 5 nodes for a 24-hour soak. If all good, schedule production cutover window.

Attachment: signed_msa_v2.pdf (PDF)

Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff + network diagram (private endpoints / on-prem)

Thanks team — confirmed for Wed 6/6 13:00–14:00 PST (calendar invite sent). Quick pre-kickoff checklist (please action before the call):

- CirrusCare: confirm VPC IDs, CIDRs, and open firewall ticket with allowlist (Alex).
- CirrusCare: share a temporary SSH jump host IP if we need to pull logs during canary (optional).
- Redwood: publish expected private endpoint IPs in INF-4821 (Marcus).
- Redwood: share a preflight runbook and test script for canary (Irene — attached link).

During the call we'll: review the network diagram, agree on peering steps (we'll handoff the peering template), confirm the allowlist, and pick a 48-hour canary window. Post-call we'll lock down the production cutover date.

Preflight link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Ccirruscare-implementation

Looking forward — Irene
